comparison: Perfect agreement. Both evaluate the same claims (C1, C35-C36, C42, C44, C48-C49, C51-C52) regarding DTX3L's ability to bind and ubiquitinate ssNAs. Both find the evidence SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm this core finding with statements like 'Solid evidence is presented' and 'evidence in strong support.'

Perfect agreement. Both evaluate the same claims (C5, C53-C55, C57-C58) regarding characterization experiments (component omission, enzyme treatments). Both find evidence SUPPORTED. Peer review notes this is part of 'detailed and diligent biochemical characterization.'

Partial disagreement. Both evaluate the same claims (C6, C75-C77, C112) regarding NMR binding data and ADPr competition. OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED, but peer review marks UNCERTAIN, noting 'NMR data could also be strengthened as the binding interface is not reported or mapped onto the structure/model.'

Perfect agreement. Both evaluate the same claims (C80-C85) regarding kinetic analysis comparing substrates. Both find evidence SUPPORTED. Peer reviewer explicitly acknowledges this addition showing 'kcat/Km is 5-fold higher for unmodified oligos.'
Perfect agreement. Both evaluate claim C43 regarding PARP9 not occluding nucleic acid binding. Both find evidence SUPPORTED. Peer review notes this data is straightforward and was not questioned.

Strong agreement with slight scope difference. OpenEval evaluates C3, C60, C63-C65, C67 (site identification experiments). Peer review evaluates C2-C3, C60, C63-C65, C67 (includes domain requirement C2). Both find evidence SUPPORTED. Peer review notes 'detailed and diligent biochemical characterization' and 'likely site of attachment.'

Strong agreement. Both evaluate overlapping claims about catalytic mechanism (C7, C86-C92 in OpenEval; C7, C86-C90, C91-C92 in peer review). Both find evidence SUPPORTED. Peer review states 'key claims made in the article are well supported by experimental data.'

Strong agreement with scope difference. OpenEval evaluates C93-C98, C106-C108 (DTX family specificity and trans-complementation). Peer review evaluates C93-C98, C102-C108 (includes structural comparison C102-C105). Both find evidence SUPPORTED. Peer review notes this addresses 'why highly related proteins do not have the same activity.'

Strong agreement. Both evaluate mechanistic model claims (C99-C101 in OpenEval; C99-C100 in peer review). Both find evidence SUPPORTED. Peer review notes this represents 'a significant expansion of our view of the ubiquitin biology.'

Strong agreement. Both evaluate extensive background/literature claims (C8-C32, C39-C41, C56, C66, C109, C111, C113, C115-C122). Both find these SUPPORTED as established facts. Peer review notes these are 'cited appropriately and not questioned.'

Strong agreement with scope difference. OpenEval evaluates C2, C45-C47 (domain deletion and catalytic activity). Peer review evaluates C45-C47, C50 (excludes C2, includes time-course C50). Both find evidence SUPPORTED. Peer review notes these validate 'catalytic competence of the truncated construct.'

Partial overlap. OpenEval evaluates C33-C34, C37-C38 (structural predictions). Peer review evaluates C33-C34, C37-C38, C109-C110, C113-C114 (includes additional N-terminal domain claims). Both find evidence SUPPORTED. Peer review notes 'no concerns were raised about the AlphaFold modeling.'

Partial overlap. OpenEval evaluates C4, C71-C73 (dsDNA overhang requirements). Peer review evaluates C4, C59, C68-C74 (broader substrate specificity including sequence preferences). Both find evidence SUPPORTED. Peer review notes this is part of 'comprehensive biochemical analysis.'

Partial overlap. OpenEval evaluates C68-C70, C74 (sequence and length preferences). Peer review evaluates C4, C59, C68-C74 (broader substrate specificity). Both find evidence SUPPORTED as part of substrate characterization.
Partial overlap. OpenEval evaluates C102-C105 (structural differences explaining specificity). Peer review evaluates C93-C98, C102-C108 (broader DTX family comparison). Both find evidence SUPPORTED.
Minimal overlap. OpenEval evaluates C50 (time-course kinetics) alone. Peer review evaluates C45-C47, C50 (catalytic controls including C50). Both find evidence SUPPORTED.

Minimal overlap. OpenEval evaluates C59 (dsDNA not ubiquitinated) with refinement note. Peer review evaluates C4, C59, C68-C74 (broader substrate specificity including C59). Both find evidence SUPPORTED.

OpenEval evaluates C61-C62 (chemical lability properties supporting ester linkage) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific chemical property claims, though related site identification (C63) is covered in peer R2.

OpenEval evaluates C78-C79 (competition assay with D31 showing overlapping binding sites) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific competition claims, though related binding claims are covered in peer R5.

Minimal overlap. OpenEval evaluates C86, C88 (DTC residue conservation from literature/structure) as SUPPORTED. Peer review evaluates C7, C86-C92 (broader catalytic mechanism including C86, C88). Both find evidence SUPPORTED.

Minimal overlap. OpenEval evaluates C110-C111, C114 (KH domain GXXG motif absence). Peer review evaluates C33-C34, C37-C38, C109-C110, C113-C114 (broader structural analysis including C110, C114). Both find evidence SUPPORTED.
